_readme: WHICH ROWS A REPO REBUILD GIVES BACK, AND WHICH ONLY A BACKUP HAS.
tests/schema-drift.mjs proves the repo rebuilds the SCHEMA and says so in its
own header: 'DATA. This proves the SCHEMA rebuilds. It says nothing about
whether any row survives a restore.' This file is the other half.
Every base table in public carries a `class`:
seeded        the repo reconstructs the rows; no backup needed. `replay` is
PINNED, so a catalogue that would rebuild to a different size
fails the guard instead of quietly running a different game.
restore_only  the repo creates the table EMPTY. Only a backup has the rows.
This is the data-loss surface, and it is what the runbook is
for. `wiped_at_cutover` says whether losing it before cutover
operational   accumulates from the database simply running. Losing it costs
observability history, never player value. Not asserted.
regenerated   rebuilds to the right COUNT and the WRONG VALUE. Exactly one
table, and it is the one a count-based census would lie about.
Classifications are AUTHORED, never generated — deciding what a restore owes
a table is a judgement, and --write preserves whatever is already here.

method: Read-only. `select count(*)` over every base table in public, in one
statement built from pg_class, executed against the live database. Not
reltuples — reltuples was wrong on two tables at this size (bug_reports
estimated 21, actual 27; maintenance_log estimated 51, actual 106), which
is the whole reason this block records exact counts.

_why: NOT asserted by the guard and NOT reconstructible from this repository.
Recorded because the runbook needs it and because auth.users is the single
most important table in the system that no migration creates.
_auth_users_is_the_root: 17 foreign keys in public reference auth.users, 12 of them ON DELETE
If auth.users is empty, none of the player rows can even be INSERTED back,
and every player has lost their account. It is carried by a Supabase
backup restore (the clone feature lists 'Auth user data' explicitly) and by
_storage_is_not_in_any_backup: Supabase documents that database backups do NOT include objects stored via
the Storage API — the database holds only metadata. One bucket, one object
at measurement. Nothing player-facing depends on it today; if that ever
changes, Storage needs its own backup and this line must stop being true.

how_to_remeasure: select string_agg(format('select %L as tbl, count(*) as n from public.%I',
c.relname, c.relname), ' union all ' order by c.relname)
from pg_class c join pg_namespace n on n.oid=c.relnamespace
…then execute the string it returns. And for outside_public:

_why: A rebuilt database that comes back without its retention jobs is a disk
with a fuse on it. game_events reached 1,598,269 rows / 229 MB from six
players in four days — 94% of a 244 MB database — and the fix was a
retention job. The guard pins every job the chain schedules by name,
schedule AND command, so a rebuild silently losing one fails the build.
expected: trim-chat-messages | 15 3 * * * | delete from public.chat_messages where created_at < now() - interval '60 days'

hearthrise-leaderboards: chain DOES schedule it on a real Postgres. The PGlite replay cannot see it,
for a structural reason worth writing down rather than working around:
2026-08-08-leaderboards.sql is the ONLY file that opens its cron block with
`create extension if not exists pg_cron`, inside a nested handler whose
`exception when others` does `return`. PGlite has no pg_cron extension — the
fixture supplies a cron SCHEMA and shim functions, not the extension — so
the create raises, the handler returns out of the whole DO block, and the
schedule never runs. Every other file guards with to_regclass('cron.job') /
PROVEN BY EXECUTION, not by reading: replaying the chain with that single
line elided produces 'hearthrise-leaderboards' and replaying it unchanged
does not. So this is a stand-in artefact, NOT a hole in the rebuild.
Consequence for the guard: it covers 8 of production's 9 jobs. It is not
listed in `expected` because a guard must not assert what it cannot observe,
and it is written down here so that '8 jobs OK' is never read as '9 covered'.
VERIFY THE NINTH BY HAND after any real rebuild:
select jobname, schedule from cron.job order by jobname;   -- expect 9

An untested backup is a rumour. This census proves which rows a restore
must carry. It does not prove Supabase gives them back — only executing the
runbook against a real restore target does that. Set `last_executed` to the
date it was run and record the measured RTO in the runbook.

beta_invites.note: 20 codes with used_by/used_at. The CODES are operator-recreatable in one INSERT; the record of WHICH are burned is not, so a restore-free rebuild re-opens every spent invite. Low value, cheap to accept.

bug_reports.note: 27 rows of player-submitted support history. No player value at stake, real diagnostic value. Survivable loss; not worth a decision at 3am.

chat_blocks.note: Per-player mute list. Empty today. Losing it silently un-mutes someone a player chose to block — small, but it is a player-authored safety setting, not telemetry.

chat_messages.note: 60-day retention job already trims this. Loss is acceptable at any time.

clan_ledger.note: Append-only clan journal; the budget source for clan_deposit clamps. Clan surface — see clans.

clans.note: ⚠ DECISION NOT RECORDED ANYWHERE. CLAUDE.md says 'the beta WILL BE WIPED at cutover' with no carve-outs, and clan standing is derived from contributions earned in the wiped client-authored economy — so `true` is the defensible reading and is what is written here. But the clan/raid/world surface was built server-authoritative FROM THE START (docs/design/server-authority.md §2), which makes it the one part of the beta that was never exploitable, and nobody has written down whether it is in or out of the wipe. Owner: Tyler + Backend Architect. Settle it BEFORE the cutover, not during it.

display_names.note: The uniqueness ledger behind 2026-08-08-unique-names.sql. This is IDENTITY, not progression: a wipe of progress does not take a player's name. Losing it frees every claimed name for re-registration by someone else, which is unrecoverable once a stranger takes it. Treat as must-restore.

game_events.note: Telemetry, 7-day retention (trim-game-events). Reached 1,598,269 rows / 229 MB — 94% of a 244 MB database — before the retention job and truncate brought it to 5,132 rows / 1,096 kB. Zero player value; total loss acceptable. It is in this census only so the retention job that keeps it small stays pinned.

game_saves.note: The client-authored blob: gold, inventory, every skill's XP, equipment, farm. 6 rows / 464 kB. server-authority.md §2a-iv is explicit — 'Starting state is FRESH. game_saves.snapshot is never read' — so a post-cutover restore has NO reason to bring it back, and reading it would launder the forged values the audit found. PRE-cutover it is every player's entire save and a total loss. This is the single table whose value flips from critical to worthless the moment the cutover completes.

hr_activities.note: Generated from src/data/*.js by tools/gen-catalogues.mjs; content guarded by --check as a smoke preflight.

hr_castle_items.note: Hand-maintained, seeded 'from src/data/items.js' BY COMMENT ONLY — server-authority.md §3.4 records it as the one catalogue tools/gen-catalogues.mjs does not own. Its migration DOES self-check, but asymmetrically: `if v_n < 34` is a FLOOR, so a catalogue that shrinks fails the migration and a catalogue that GROWS applies clean. The exact count pinned here is the only guard covering the second direction — proven by the shrink/grow mutation pair in tests/restore-census.mjs, which are caught by different mechanisms on purpose.

hr_catalogue_meta.note: The catalogue digest row; the generator's own fingerprint.

hr_client_rpc_baseline.note: The approved client-callable RPC list. hr_assert_grant_hygiene check (2) raises on any grant not recorded here, nightly on cron. A rebuild that seeded a different set would make that detector wrong in both directions.

hr_items.note: Generated catalogue — the market tradeable allowlist. 15 untradeable. Content digest d10936764d0e…, guarded by tools/gen-catalogues.mjs --check.

hr_rate_counters.note: Unlogged rate-limit counters. 104 in production, 2 in a rebuild (the migrations' own self-checks spend budget). Losing them resets every rate window to empty — the correct failure direction, and self-healing within a minute.

hr_rejections.note: Sampled hr_apply rejections, pruned by cron. Anomaly-detection history only.

hr_server_secrets.note: A REBUILD PRODUCES ONE ROW WITH A DIFFERENT VALUE. 2026-08-11-player-state.sql seeds it with sha256(gen_random_uuid()||gen_random_uuid()||clock_timestamp()), so the 256-bit PRNG secret is FRESH on every apply. A count-based census reports this table as reconstructed; it is not. What changes if the value changes: (1) hr_seed's accrual PRNG re-rolls, so a disputed drop can no longer be replayed deterministically from player_ledger — the stated reason the seed is deterministic at all; (2) the accrual idempotency key hr_seed(user,slot,'intent:accrue:<watermark>') moves, so an in-flight accrual retried across the boundary is no longer deduplicated and can pay twice — bounded, because accrued_to is restored with it and hr_apply re-validates against the restored watermark. Neither is fatal. Both are silent. A restore from a BACKUP keeps the real value; only a repo rebuild re-rolls it.

hr_start_equipment.note: Generated from src/data/start-kit.js. A divergence here means server-created characters start with different gear than the client shows — a live bug this file's guard chain already caught once (0 gold, no weapon, into server-side combat).

hr_xp_table.note: The XP curve, 99 levels, with 3 anchor assertions in the migration.

leaderboard_meta.note: Board namespace metadata. The board itself, leaderboard_ranked, is a MATERIALIZED VIEW — derived, not stored, and recomputed by hr_leaderboard_refresh; it is correctly absent from this census.

maintenance_alerts.note: hr_cron_health output. Losing it loses alert history, not the alerts.

maintenance_log.note: Retention/cron run log. 106 rows in production, 2 in a rebuild.

market_buy_offers.note: Legacy market. 2026-08-11-market-v2.sql drops and recreates the market tables; the old economy is discarded at cutover by design.

market_listings.note: Legacy market — see market_buy_offers. NOTE: under market v2 a listing row IS the seller's escrowed goods, so once v2 ships this table stops being disposable and this classification must be revisited in the same change.

player_equipment.note: POST-CUTOVER PROGRESSION. Empty today. After cutover the database is the only copy and a repo rebuild returns this empty.

player_intents.note: 24-hour idempotency window, pruned hourly by hr-intents-prune. Losing it means a retry inside the window is no longer deduplicated — bounded by the same version/watermark checks hr_apply already makes.

player_inventory.note: POST-CUTOVER PROGRESSION. Empty today. One row per item; the bank cap is count(*) over it.

player_ledger.note: POST-CUTOVER PROGRESSION AND THE AUDIT TRAIL. 3 rows today. Append-only by trigger (UPDATE, TRUNCATE and in-window DELETE all refused). It is the source of every daily budget: hr_day_budget_used SUMS this table rather than reading a counter, so restoring player_state WITHOUT player_ledger silently resets every player's daily gold/XP/item ceiling to zero-used — a restore that grants a second full day of budget. Restore the two together or not at all.

player_ledger_rollup.note: Aggregates written by hr_ledger_prune as it deletes aged ledger rows. Derived — but NOT re-derivable once the source rows are pruned. Losing it loses history beyond the ledger window, never live state.

player_progress.note: POST-CUTOVER PROGRESSION — quests, dailies, bounties, stats, collections, flags. Empty today.

player_skills.note: POST-CUTOVER PROGRESSION — XP per skill, the value every level and every leaderboard score is derived from. Empty today.

player_state.note: POST-CUTOVER PROGRESSION — gold, gems, hearth_tokens, hp, the activity pointer, version. Empty today. THE row every write locks. After cutover this table has no second copy anywhere in the world.

profiles.note: IDENTITY, not progression: display name derived server-side for chat and the market. 8 rows. Losing it makes every player 'Adventurer' and breaks name authority until each player re-registers a name.

raid_claims.note: Clan surface — see clans. Empty today. Its purpose is to make a raid reward unclaimable twice, so losing it re-opens every past claim; empty means nothing is at stake right now.

session_claims.note: Single-active-session heartbeat rows, keyed on the tab. Self-healing: a lost claim is re-taken on the next heartbeat. Losing them cannot lock a player out (save-invariant #2 — eviction requires a definitive fresh-heartbeat row, and absence is not that).

world_event_joins.note: World-event surface — same open decision as clans.

world_event_pledges.note: World-event surface — same open decision as clans.

world_event_totals.note: World-event surface — same open decision as clans.
